# `silk/collections/hash_map`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Hash maps that own their keys and values, with deterministic seeded hashing.

## When to use
Use [`HashMap`](#HashMap) to find a value by a key. The key type must implement `silk.collections.hash.HashKey`. Use
`silk.collections.list.List` when the order of insertion matters, or when the code finds values by position.

## Details
[`HashMap.make`](#HashMap.impl.make) does not allocate. The first insert allocates eight buckets.
[`HashMap.makeWithCapacity`](#HashMap.impl.makeWithCapacity) and [`HashMap.reserve`](#HashMap.impl.reserve) allocate room for a known number of entries
in one step. [`HashMap.clear`](#HashMap.impl.clear) drops the entries and keeps the buckets for reuse, and
[`HashMap.clearAndFree`](#HashMap.impl.clearAndFree) also releases them. The map rebuilds its table before more than three
quarters of the buckets are in use. A bucket stays in use after a removal, until the next
rebuild. The rebuild doubles the number of buckets if the entries fill more than half of them.
Otherwise it keeps the number and only clears the removed buckets, so a map that inserts and
removes forever keeps a bucket count in proportion to its largest length. A failed growth leaves
the entries, the length, and the bucket count unchanged.

The same seed and the same operations give the same bucket order on each target. To visit each
entry, scan the buckets from 0 to [`HashMap.bucketCount`](#HashMap.impl.bucketCount), test [`HashMap.occupiedAt`](#HashMap.impl.occupiedAt), and read
[`HashMap.keyAt`](#HashMap.impl.keyAt) and [`HashMap.valueAt`](#HashMap.impl.valueAt). This order is the bucket order, not the order of
insertion.

## Gotchas
Each lookup and removal consumes its probe key. [`HashMap.get`](#HashMap.impl.get), [`HashMap.keyAt`](#HashMap.impl.keyAt), and
[`HashMap.valueAt`](#HashMap.impl.valueAt) copy, so the key and value types must be `Copy`. For a value that is not
`Copy`, use [`HashMap.withMut`](#HashMap.impl.withMut) to change it in place, or [`HashMap.remove`](#HashMap.impl.remove) to move it out.

## Examples
### Insert, read, and remove one value
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.collections.hash { Hash, Word }
import silk.collections.hash_map { HashMap }
import silk.core.option { Option }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut map = HashMap<Word, i32>.make(Hash.seed(17))
  let previous = run HashMap<Word, i32>.insert(&mut map, Hash.word(7), 42)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let found = HashMap<Word, i32>.get(&map, Hash.word(7)) |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(0)
  let removed = HashMap<Word, i32>.remove(&mut map, Hash.word(7)) |> Option<i32>.unwrapOr(0)
  if found != 42 || removed != 42 || HashMap<Word, i32>.contains(&map, Hash.word(7)) {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `HashMap` with `import silk.collections.hash_map { HashMap }`.

<a id="HashMap"></a>

## `HashMap`

```silk
pub struct HashMap<K, V>
```

A hash map that owns unique keys and their values, with deterministic seeded hashing.

### When to use

Use it to find a value by a key. The key type must implement `silk.collections.hash.HashKey`. Use
`silk.collections.list.List` when the order of insertion matters, or when the code finds values by
position.

### Details

[`HashMap.make`](#HashMap.impl.make) does not allocate. The first insert allocates eight buckets.
[`HashMap.makeWithCapacity`](#HashMap.impl.makeWithCapacity) and [`HashMap.reserve`](#HashMap.impl.reserve) allocate room for a known number of entries
in one step. [`HashMap.clear`](#HashMap.impl.clear) drops the entries and keeps the buckets for reuse, and
[`HashMap.clearAndFree`](#HashMap.impl.clearAndFree) also releases them. The map rebuilds its table before more than three
quarters of the buckets are in use. A bucket stays in use after a removal, until the next
rebuild. The rebuild doubles the number of buckets if the entries fill more than half of them.
Otherwise it keeps the number and only clears the removed buckets, so a map that inserts and
removes forever keeps a bucket count in proportion to its largest length. A failed growth leaves
the entries, the length, and the bucket count unchanged.

To visit each entry, scan the buckets from 0 to [`HashMap.bucketCount`](#HashMap.impl.bucketCount), test
[`HashMap.occupiedAt`](#HashMap.impl.occupiedAt), and read [`HashMap.keyAt`](#HashMap.impl.keyAt) and [`HashMap.valueAt`](#HashMap.impl.valueAt). This order is the
bucket order, not the order of insertion. The same seed and the same operations give the same
bucket order on each target.

Each key is unique under `HashKey.equals`. An insert with a key that is already present replaces
the value. The map uses one seed for all of its hashes. Dropping the map drops each key and
value and then releases the storage.

### Gotchas

Each lookup and removal consumes its probe key. [`HashMap.get`](#HashMap.impl.get), [`HashMap.keyAt`](#HashMap.impl.keyAt), and
[`HashMap.valueAt`](#HashMap.impl.valueAt) copy, so the key and value types must be `Copy`. For a value that is not
`Copy`, use [`HashMap.withMut`](#HashMap.impl.withMut) to change it in place, or [`HashMap.remove`](#HashMap.impl.remove) to move it out.

<a id="HashMap.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(seed: HashSeed) -> HashMap<K, V>
```

Returns an empty map that uses `seed` for each hash. This function does not allocate.

#### Details

The seed and the sequence of operations decide the bucket order.

<a id="HashMap.impl.makeWithCapacity"></a>

### Associated function `makeWithCapacity`

```silk
pub effect fn makeWithCapacity(seed: HashSeed, capacity: usize) -> HashMap<K, V>
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns an empty map that uses `seed` for each hash, with buckets for at least `capacity`
entries before the first rebuild.

#### When to use

Use `makeWithCapacity` when the number of entries is known or can be estimated before the
inserts, so that the table allocates once instead of growing step by step.

#### Details

The length is 0. Inserts of up to `capacity` entries do not allocate. The bucket count is the
smallest of 8, 16, 32, and so on that keeps `capacity` entries under three quarters of the
buckets. A `capacity` of 0 does not allocate and gives the same map as [`HashMap.make`](#HashMap.impl.make). The
seed and the sequence of operations decide the bucket order.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the bucket count overflows `usize`, or the `Allocator` cannot supply
  the storage.

<a id="HashMap.impl.insert"></a>

### Method `insert`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn insert<K: HashKey + 'env, 'env>(
    self: &mut Self,
    key: K,
    value: V
  ) -> Option<V> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Inserts `key` with `value`. Returns the old value if the map already held an equal key, or
`None`.

#### Details

The map takes ownership of `key` and `value`. If an equal key is already present, the length
does not change: the map keeps the new key and value, drops the old key, and returns the old
value.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the table must grow and the `Allocator` cannot supply the storage. The
  map does not change.

```silk
pub fn contains<K: HashKey>(self: &Self, key: K) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if the map holds a key equal to `key`.

#### Details

This function consumes `key`. It does not change the map.

<a id="HashMap.impl.indexOf"></a>

### Method `indexOf`

```silk
pub fn indexOf<K: HashKey>(self: &Self, key: K) -> Option<usize>
```

Returns the bucket index of the entry with a key equal to `key`, or `None` if there is no such
entry.

#### When to use

Use `indexOf` to find a key without a copy or a move, for example when the value type is not
`Copy`.

#### Details

This function consumes `key`. It does not change the map.

<a id="HashMap.impl.get"></a>

### Method `get`

```silk
pub fn get<K: HashKey + Copy, V: Copy>(self: &Self, key: K) -> Option<V>
```

Returns a copy of the value for the key equal to `key`, or `None` if there is no such key.

#### When to use

Use `get` when the key and value types are `Copy`. Use [`HashMap.withMut`](#HashMap.impl.withMut) or
[`HashMap.remove`](#HashMap.impl.remove) for a value that is not `Copy`.

#### Details

This function consumes `key`. It does not change the map.

<a id="HashMap.impl.withMut"></a>

### Method `withMut`

```silk
pub fn withMut<K: HashKey, F: once fn(&mut V) -> () + Intrinsic.NonParking
  >(self: &mut Self, key: K, use: F) -> bool
```

Calls `use` one time with an exclusive borrow of the value for the key equal to `key`. Returns
`false` and does not call `use` if there is no such key.

#### When to use

Use `withMut` to change a value in place, such as to increment a counter, when the value type
is not `Copy`.

#### Details

This function does not allocate and does not grow the map. It consumes `key`. The stored key,
the length, and the bucket count do not change. `use` returns `()`, so it cannot keep the
borrow.

#### Gotchas

`use` must be `Intrinsic.NonParking`. It cannot suspend.

<a id="HashMap.impl.remove"></a>

### Method `remove`

```silk
pub fn remove<K: HashKey>(self: &mut Self, key: K) -> Option<V>
```

Removes the entry with a key equal to `key` and returns its value. Returns `None` if there is
no such entry.

#### Details

The caller owns the returned value. The stored key is dropped. This function consumes `key`.
It does not allocate.

<a id="HashMap.impl.keyAt"></a>

### Method `keyAt`

```silk
pub fn keyAt<K: Copy, V: Copy>(self: &Self, index: usize) -> K
```

Returns a copy of the key in the bucket at `index`.

#### When to use

Use `keyAt` with [`HashMap.occupiedAt`](#HashMap.impl.occupiedAt) to visit each entry in bucket order.

#### Gotchas

The key and value types must be `Copy`. If `index` is out of range or the bucket is empty, the
program traps.


Returns a copy of the value in the bucket at `index`.

#### When to use

Use `valueAt` with [`HashMap.occupiedAt`](#HashMap.impl.occupiedAt) to visit each entry in bucket order.

#### Gotchas

The key and value types must be `Copy`. If `index` is out of range or the bucket is empty, the
program traps.

<a id="HashMap.impl.reserve"></a>

### Method `reserve`

```silk
pub effect fn reserve(self: &mut Self, additional: usize) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Makes sure that at least `additional` more entries fit before the next rebuild.

#### When to use

Use `reserve` before a run of inserts whose count is known, so that the table grows at most
once.

#### Details

If the buckets already hold `additional` more entries under three quarters of the bucket
count, this function does nothing. Otherwise, it rebuilds the table once, with the smallest
bucket count, doubling from the current one or from 8, that holds the length plus `additional`
entries. The rebuild also reclaims the buckets of removed entries. The length does not change.
An
`additional` of 0 does nothing.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the length plus `additional` overflows `usize`, the bucket count
  overflows `usize`, or the `Allocator` cannot supply the storage. The map does not change.

<a id="HashMap.impl.clear"></a>

### Method `clear`

```silk
pub fn clear(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Drops every entry and sets the length to 0. The bucket count does not change.

#### When to use

Use `clear` to reuse a map, such as one filled again on each pass of a loop: later inserts up
to the old size do not allocate. Use [`HashMap.clearAndFree`](#HashMap.impl.clearAndFree) to also release the storage.

#### Details

The buckets of removed entries are reclaimed too. This function does not allocate.

<a id="HashMap.impl.clearAndFree"></a>

### Method `clearAndFree`

```silk
pub fn clearAndFree(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Drops every entry and releases the storage. The length and the bucket count become 0.

#### When to use

Use `clearAndFree` when the map stays alive but its storage is no longer needed. Use
[`HashMap.clear`](#HashMap.impl.clear) to keep the buckets for reuse.

#### Details

This function does not allocate and does not need an `Allocator`. The next insert allocates
eight buckets again, as on a map from [`HashMap.make`](#HashMap.impl.make). The seed does not change.
